    PRODUCT AND PROTOCOL

    Hookline docs

    What works now, how the evidence is built, and the path from contract desk to hook infrastructure.

    GitHub
    01 / PRODUCT

    The intelligence layer for onchain hooks

    Hookline organizes live contract evidence around one chain-aware identity, then makes the record useful through watchlists, comparisons, monitoring, and developer access.

    Observe

    Read deployed bytecode, fingerprint the runtime, probe conventional ownership, decode permissions, and retain the observed block.

    Monitor

    Save named local watchlists, refresh evidence intentionally, preserve successful history, and surface failures without erasing prior state.

    Build

    Consume the same evidence through constrained JSON-RPC and a machine-payable x402 capacity route.

    Current boundary: Discovery and aggregate counts use a timestamped community snapshot. Project profiles add pinned contract reads and selected decoded events, with coverage and source blocks attached. This is not complete swap, fee, or payout history.

    02 / DATA MODEL

    Evidence before interpretation

    Contract identity is always chain ID + normalized address. Each successful observation retains chain, address, block, timestamp, bytecode size, runtime fingerprint, permission state, owner-probe result, and latency.

    DIRECTRPC bytecode, calls, blocks, logs, and transactions
    DERIVEDpermission flags, fingerprints, normalized identities, and event aggregates
    VERIFIEDsource verification and signed external metadata with attribution
    SUBMITTEDproject descriptions, links, and manifests labeled as project claims

    A failed refresh remains a failure. It never becomes empty successful evidence and never overwrites the most recent valid observation.

    03 / API

    One evidence surface for people and agents

    Hookline methods

    • hookline_chainssupported networks and upstreams
    • hookline_decodePermissionscanonical low-14-bit permission state
    • hookline_chainStatusidentity, height, status, and latency
    • hookline_getHooklive evidence for one chain and address
    POST /rpc
    {
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "hookline_getHook",
  "params": [8453, "0xb082…6888"],
  "id": 1
}

    The free route is rate limited. POST /rpc/paid requests 0.01 USDC on Base through x402. The proxy rejects transaction submission, account access, administrative, debug, trace, and batch requests.

    04 / WHITEPAPER

    An evidence and coordination layer for hooks

    Programmable-liquidity hooks create a discovery problem. Deployments, permissions, code versions, owners, pool relationships, activity, and project claims live across tools that do not treat the hook as a first-class research object.

    Hookline’s job is to make it easy to answer what a hook is, where it is deployed, what it can do, what depends on it, what changed, and where the evidence came from.
    HOOKS,POOLS,CHAINS,DEPLOYERS,CODE,EVENTS

    The board is the map. The Hook Tape now owns finalized Base pool-initialization and live swap evidence with exact source transactions. Swap rows retain signed pool deltas, the fee PoolManager emitted, and normalized relevant ERC-20 transfers from successful receipts when available. Those transfers are not automatically fees. Traces come next for refusals and call-path attribution.

    Read the complete whitepaper on GitHub
    05 / ROADMAP

    Build usefulness before surface area

    1. NOW

      Projects and first-party Hook Tape

      Broad project discovery, source-linked contract evidence, finalized Base pool births and live swaps, exact source transactions, project follows, submissions, and reviewed user-wallet execution.

    2. NEXT

      Trace-backed outcomes and change intelligence

      Separate hook-flow and refusal evidence, recipients, implementation changes, and bytecode-family alerts.

    3. AFTER

      Deeper route evidence

      Pool price versus hook-adjusted result, measurable fee deltas, refusal evidence, and recipient flows inside the existing user-wallet execution receipt.

    4. LATER

      Professional and ecosystem layers

      Team workspaces, webhooks, longer retention, signed manifests, contributed research, and additional programmable-liquidity systems.

    06 / FAQ

    Frequently asked questions

    Where does Hookline data come from?

    The hook board uses a timestamped v4.xyz community-indexer snapshot for discovery and aggregate pool and swap counts. Names and descriptions are community-curated or project-submitted. Live contract evidence comes directly from configured Ethereum, BNB Chain, Base, Arbitrum One, and Robinhood Chain RPC endpoints.

    Why does the index snapshot show an older time?

    It shows when the discovery and aggregate-count snapshot was generated by the index-sync job. It does not update on each page load and is not the timestamp of every market quote or contract read. Those have their own observation times.

    What is the Projects board?

    A broader view of hook-powered projects and infrastructure, separate from individual hooks or tokens. A project can have several deployments or no token. Each profile separates sourced descriptions, team updates, saved contract reads, and observed changes.

    How are Board, Observe, and Watchlists different?

    Board discovers indexed hooks and tokens. Observe inspects an address directly on a selected chain, even if it is not indexed. Watchlists save selected contracts, local evidence history, and same-chain comparisons.

    Do configured allocations prove a payout happened?

    No. CLAUS configurations, accrued balances, buyback/burn records, liquidity additions, and NFT rewards are separate facts. A confirmed burn transfer requires the exact token transfer in the same successful transaction receipt. Other events remain contract-reported. ENGRAM accrued fees stay accrued. These are bounded observations, not lifetime totals or proof of financial benefit.

    Can I submit or claim a project?

    Yes, free, through the project form, API, or Telegram bot. Suggestions enter private agent review. Claiming requires a DNS TXT record on the researched project domain. Domain control allows profile-copy updates, not edits to chain evidence or a safety badge. No email or HKLN holding is required.

    How do project alerts work?

    Follow a project in Telegram. A bounded scanner checks monitored deployments on a rotating 10-minute schedule and shares the same evidence records used on the site. Per-target timing varies; profiles show source blocks and scan coverage. Initial historical reads do not become new-activity alerts.

    Does every project have complete monitoring?

    No. Listed projects, sourced deployments, selected monitoring targets, and successful observations are separate counts. Profiles show source blocks, last successful reads, and event lag. A listed name or domain claim is not a safety endorsement or proof of complete history.

    Does Hookline show volume and liquidity?

    Yes. Related markets show available DexScreener price, market cap, liquidity, volume, and change alongside the indexed relationship. The first-party Tape separately keeps a bounded finalized Base swap feed for already-resolved hooked pools; it is not complete historical volume. Missing data stays unavailable. Liquidity alerts require complete readings for the same indexed pool set.

    What does a Dynamic pool fee mean?

    It identifies Uniswap v4's dynamic-fee configuration flag, not an 838.8608% fee or a measured current fee. Static advertised LP fees, adaptive LP fees, hook charges, and Hookline execution fees stay separate. Swap-specific evidence is required to measure what was actually paid.

    What does Velocity mean?

    Velocity ranks the current indexed activity density of each hook or token relationship. It is a discovery ranking, not a promise of future performance.

    What is the Hook Tape?

    It is a first-party Base feed with separate Swaps and Pool births views. Pool rows prove the hook relationship and fee configuration at initialization. Swap rows retain signed pool deltas, the fee PoolManager emitted, post-swap state, finalized block, and source transaction for already-resolved hooked pools. Successful receipt enrichment keeps only bounded ERC-20 transfers touching the hook or a pool currency. A transfer is observable flow, not automatic proof of a fee or its economic purpose. Activity cards summarize an explicit retained block window and label partial coverage. Raw swaps are capped at seven days and 200,000 rows to keep storage predictable. Rejected attempts and call-path attribution require traces.

    What does the Telegram bot do?

    Explore hook relationships, markets, and project follows. Alert cards show sourced names, chain, full copyable contract addresses, and Details/Pause/Resume buttons. Add alert, Projects, Settings, and Main menu reduce command typing. Hook alerts check runtime changes, new finalized Base PoolManager relationships, PoolManager-reported fee moves of at least 10 basis points for the same finalized pool, new community-indexed relationships, and qualifying liquidity changes on the 10-minute schedule. Fee alerts carry before/after rates, pool ID, block, and source transaction without calling that rate a hook charge. Existing subscriptions seed silently; historical backfill never becomes a false new-pool alert. Telegram does not sign; reviewed execution opens on the website for your wallet.

    What does Hookline execution cost?

    Hookline shows a 1% gross execution fee and applies 0.3% cashback instantly in the route, leaving a 0.7% effective fee. There is no deferred cashback claim. The public RPC never submits a transaction. The user’s wallet signs and submits the exact reviewed route, then Hookline independently verifies the receipt.

    Can I save trade settings?

    Slippage and buy/sell presets are supported. Website settings stay on that device; Telegram settings belong to the private Telegram identity. A trade link carries its explicit settings, never an automatic signature. Native amounts are not silently converted to wrapped-token or stablecoin units. Priority remains wallet-managed; saved TP/SL profiles are not active orders.

    Will Hookline support user-owned smart wallets?

    That is the planned automated-order design, not a live wallet service. Users retain owner and recovery control. Any automation needs explicit, revocable, expiring permissions with asset, router, recipient, and spending limits. Transfers, bridges, and ownership changes need separate authority. Wallet creation and automatic limit or TP/SL orders are not enabled.

    Does Trade guarantee a route through this hook?

    No. A reviewed aggregator quote may use other pools, and some custom hooks are unsupported. Hook-specific routing is not verified. An unsupported route stops; the displayed project or hook is not an execution guarantee.

    Do I need a Hookline account?

    No. Research stays anonymous. Optional wallet-message sign-in lets you save list names, addresses, and trade preferences to a private account and load them on another device. Sign-in costs no gas and grants no spending permission. It does not create a wallet or place an order.

    Can I create a wallet here?

    Open Wallets, sign in, then choose Create my wallet. Google, email, and external wallets are available; the picker shows only enabled methods. Return with the same login to use the same embedded EVM wallet. Different unlinked logins can create separate accounts. Export opens Privy's secure interface. Each signature needs your confirmation, gas is not sponsored, and automated orders are not active. Apple sign-in is not offered.

    What do the 14 permission flags prove?

    They identify which Uniswap v4 callback permissions are encoded in the hook address. They do not explain the complete runtime behavior and do not establish that a contract is safe.

    Is this a smart-contract audit?

    No. Hookline is an evidence and monitoring product, not an audit, legal opinion, or trading recommendation.

    Why can’t I compare live state across chains?

    An address is not a complete identity, and block heights on separate chains do not share state or time semantics. Hookline limits direct comparisons to one chain.

    Are watchlists uploaded?

    Only when you choose Save to account. Names and addresses are saved, not raw local observations. Load keeps matching local history and backs up the previous device copy. Project monitoring history and Telegram follows are stored separately so alerts do not depend on an open browser.

    What does linking Telegram do?

    A single-use, expiring link connects your private Telegram identity to your website account. It does not merge settings, delete alerts, or grant trading authority. Sign-out keeps the device copy; Clear device copy removes local data without deleting account data or Telegram alerts.

    Does the RPC submit transactions?

    No. Transaction submission and account-access methods are rejected by the public service.

    What is the x402 route?

    It is a machine-payable capacity path. A valid unpaid request receives an HTTP 402 challenge for 0.01 USDC on Base.

    Does market cap generate Hookline revenue?

    No. Market cap itself does not create creator fees. Venue fees require trading activity, and product revenue requires useful paid services.

    Is Hookline affiliated with Uniswap or Robinhood?

    No. Hookline is independent and is not endorsed by Uniswap Labs, Robinhood, Flaunch, PayAI, or its RPC providers.

    How can I contribute?

    Use Submit a project or Suggest correction on the Projects board, or send /submitproject or /suggest in Telegram. For code and evidence bugs, use GitHub with the chain, address, source block, and reproduction steps.
